## Negative product: choose opposite signs {.psf-lesson .split-example}

The number farther from zero takes the sign of the sum. For a sum of $1$ or $-1$, look for absolute values one apart.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$2x^2+x-6$

::: {.fragment}

$P=-12$, $S=1$: the number farther from zero is positive.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Pair | $-1,\ 12$ | $-2,\ 6$ | $-3,\ 4$ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Sum | $11$ | $4$ | $1$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

Choose $-3,4$: $-3+4=1$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=2x^2+4x-3x-6$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=2x(x+2)-3(x+2)$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=(2x-3)(x+2)$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$2x^2-x-6$

1. Predict the signs.
2. Choose the pair.
3. Split and group on paper.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$P=-12$, $S=-1$: the number farther from zero is negative.

:::

::: {.fragment}

| Pair | $1,\ -12$ | $2,\ -6$ | $3,\ -4$ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Sum | $-11$ | $-4$ | $-1$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

Choose $3,-4$: $3-4=-1$.

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=2x^2-4x+3x-6$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=2x(x-2)+3(x-2)$

:::

::: {.fragment}

$=(2x+3)(x-2)$

:::

:::::

::::::
